   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">IRC Sections <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">383</em> provide an annual limitation with respect to the ability of a corporation to utilize its tax attributes, as well as certain built-in-losses, against future U.S. taxable income in the event of a change in ownership. Our emergence from Chapter <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> bankruptcy proceedings in <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> is considered a change in ownership for purposes of IRC Section&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">382.</em> The merger with GulfMark in <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> resulted in a change in ownership of GulfMark for purposes of IRC Section <em style="font: inherit;">382.</em> The GulfMark ownership change results in an annual limitation of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057517" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-GulfMarkOffshoreIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="tdw:AnnualLimitationOfCompanysOwnershipChange" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million on GulfMark&#8217;s tax attributes generated prior to the ownership change date, which begin to expire in <em style="font: inherit;">2035.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management assesses the available positive and negative evidence to estimate whether sufficient future taxable income will be generated to permit the use of the existing deferred tax assets.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Based on this evaluation, for the period ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057519" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">332.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was recorded against our net deferred tax asset. For the period ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>, a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057520" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">533.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was recorded against our net deferred tax asset. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;we recorded non-cash&#160;deferred tax benefits totaling&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141057521" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="tdw:NoncashDeferredTaxBenefits" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">201.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, primarily related to a release of a valuation allowance in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and as a result of a strategic internal restructuring of our&#160;vessel ownership (Vessel Realignment) in the <em style="font: inherit;">fourth</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The valuation allowance previously established against the net U.S. deferred tax asset position was released after considering all available evidence, including the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year cumulative financial taxable income position and the domestic tax impact given our current operating structure, and determining that sufficient positive evidence existed to conclude that a&#160;portion of the valuation allowance was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer needed. We intend to maintain a valuation allowance on the remaining U.S. foreign tax credits and net deferred tax asset balances in foreign jurisdictions until sufficient evidence supports a reversal. This tax benefit is included&#160;as a component of income tax benefit in our Consolidated Income Statement&#160;for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized a U.S. deferred tax liability associated with temporary differences related to investments in our non-U.S. holding companies as we do&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to dispose of the stock of these companies. These differences relate primarily to stock basis differences attributable to factors other than earnings, given that any untaxed cumulative earnings were subject to taxation in the U.S. in <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> in accordance with the Tax Act. Further, any post-<em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> earnings of these subsidiaries will either be taxed currently for U.S. purposes or will be permanently exempt from U.S. taxation. It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practicable to estimate the deferred tax liability associated with temporary differences related to investments in our non-U.S. holding companies due to the legal structure and complexity of U.S. and non-U.S. tax laws.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Historically, it has been our practice and intention to indefinitely reinvest the earnings of its non-U.S. subsidiaries. Considering the significant changes made by the Tax Act, we will <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer be indefinitely reinvested with regards to its non-U.S. earnings which can be repatriated free of taxation. However, we are&#160;indefinitely reinvested in the non-U.S. earnings that could be subject to taxation and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> deferred taxes have been provided for such earnings. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the non-U.S. positive unremitted earnings, for which we are indefinitely reinvested, are $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057535" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UndistributedEarningsOfForeignSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">320.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practicable to estimate the amount of taxes on positive unremitted earnings due to the legal structure and complexity of non-U.S. tax laws. We decide&#160;each period whether to indefinitely reinvest these earnings. If, as a result of these reassessments, we distribute&#160;these earnings in the future, additional tax liabilities could result.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We record uncertain tax positions on the basis of a <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-step process in which (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) we determine whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the tax positions will be sustained on the basis of the technical merits of the position and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) for those tax positions that meet the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold, we recognize the largest amount of tax benefit that is more than <em style="font: inherit;">50</em> percent likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement with the related tax authority. The recognition and measurement of tax liabilities for uncertain tax positions in any tax jurisdiction requires the interpretation of the related tax laws and regulations as well as the use of estimates and assumptions regarding significant future events. Changes in tax laws, regulations, agreements and treaties, foreign currency exchange restrictions or our level of operations or profitability in each taxing jurisdiction could have an impact on the amount of income taxes during any given year.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

Certain leases include <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more options to renew with renewal terms that can extend the lease term from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057559">one</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057560">twenty-six</span> years. The exercise of lease renewal options is at our sole discretion and lease renewal options are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in our lease terms if they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reasonably certain to be exercised. Our lease agreements generally do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contain any residual value guarantees or restrictive covenants.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Defined Benefit Pension Plan </b></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have a defined benefit pension plan (pension plan) that covers certain U.S. employees. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2010, </em>the pension plan was frozen and accrual of benefits was discontinued. We&#160;contributed $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057610" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057611" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million to the plan in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively, but&#160;did <em style="font: inherit;"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057927">not</span></em> contribute to the plan during the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023. </em>We expect to contribute&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141057615" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedFutureEmployerContributionsNextFiscalYear" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to this plan in <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

     During the

    $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057619" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2023-06-30_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligationPaymentForSettlement" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of the pension plan&#8217;s pension liabilities. Under the terms of this agreement, we&#160;irrevocably transferred to the Insurer all future pension plan benefit obligations for approximately&#160;
    <em style="font: inherit;">500</em> Tidewater participants (Transferred Participants) effective in
    <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2023. </em>This annuity transaction was funded entirely with existing pension plan assets. The Insurer assumed responsibility for administrative and customer service support of the pension plan, including distribution of payments to the Transferred Participants. We recognized a
    $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057621" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2023-06-30_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementBenefitsExpenseReversalOfExpenseNoncash" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million settlement gain in the

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We offered a non-contributory, defined benefit supplemental executive retirement plan (supplemental plan) that provides pension benefits to certain employees in excess of those allowed under our tax-qualified pension plan. The supplemental plan was closed to new participation in <em style="font: inherit;">2010</em> and was frozen effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2018. </em>We contributed $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057631" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057632" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057633" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.6</ix:nonFraction> million for each of the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. Any future accrual of benefits under the supplemental plan or other contributions to the supplemental plan will be determined at our sole discretion.&#160;We expect to contribute $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057636" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedFutureEmployerContributionsNextFiscalYear" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to this plan in <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Investment Strategies </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><i>U.S. Pension Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The obligations of our pension plan are supported by assets held in a trust for the payment of benefits. We are obligated to adequately fund the trust. For the pension plan assets, we have the following primary investment objectives: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;closely match the cash flows from interest payments and maturities of the pension plan&#8217;s investments with the long-term financial&#160;obligations from the plan&#8217;s liabilities; and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;enhance the pension plan&#8217;s investment returns without taking on undue risk by industries, maturities or geographies of the underlying investment holdings.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The pension plan portfolio is broadly diversified across equity, fixed income and alternative investments. The weightings of the equity portfolio will follow the MSCI All County World Index. The fixed income portion of the pension plan will allocate at least <em style="font: inherit;">75%</em> of assets to investment-grade bonds. Alternative investments are allowed to be made. Low-liquidity alternative assets are also permitted but will have an overall target of less than <ix:nonFraction id="c141057641" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tdw:DefinedBenefitPlanConcentrationRiskAssetsEquitySecuritiesDifferencePlanAssetsAndLiabilities" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% of the asset allocation.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The cash flow requirements of the pension plan are analyzed at least annually. The pension plan does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> invest in Tidewater stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our policy for the pension plan is to contribute <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> less than the minimum required contribution by law and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> more than the maximum deductible amount. The pension plan assets are periodically evaluated for concentration risks.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Fair Value of Pension Plans Assets </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Tidewater&#8217;s pension plan assets are accounted for at fair value and are classified within the fair value hierarchy based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement, except for investments for which fair value is measured using the net asset value per share expedient.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Upon meeting various citizenship, age and service requirements, employees are eligible to participate in a defined contribution savings plan and can contribute from <ix:nonFraction id="c141057665" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tdw:DefinedContributionPlanPercentContributedByEmployeeMinimum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c141057666" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">75</ix:nonFraction>% of their base salary to an employee benefit trust.&#160;Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> October 31, 2021, </em>we matched, in cash, <ix:nonFraction id="c141057667" contextRef="d_2021-10-31_2021-10-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercentOfMatch" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> <ix:nonFraction id="c141057669" contextRef="d_2021-10-31_2021-10-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6</ix:nonFraction>% of eligible compensation deferred by the employee. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, we contributed $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057672" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057673" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057674" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DefinedContributionSavingPlanA401KMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanContributionsByEmployer" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Restricted Stock Units&#160;and Restricted Stock Awards</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have granted RSUs to key employees, including officers and non-employee directors,&#160;along with RSAs to certain non-employee directors.&#160;We have generally awarded time-based units, where each unit represents the right to receive, at the end of a vesting period, <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> unrestricted share of Tidewater common stock with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> exercise price.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We&#160;have also awarded performance-based RSUs that measure certain performance criteria or market based criteria, where each unit represents the right to receive, at the end of a service period, between <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> shares of Tidewater common stock, depending on the level of achievement of the performance criteria or defined market condition and the completion of the service requirement, with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> exercise price based on various operating and financial metrics. The fair value of the time-based RSUs is based on the market price of our common stock on the date of grant and, in the case&#160;of performance based RSUs, on the estimated level of achievement expected to be realized. For the performance based RSUs that contain a market condition, the fair value of the awards are estimated using a lattice based Monte Carlo simulation. The restrictions on the time-based RSUs awarded to key employees lapse over a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year period from the date of the award. The restrictions on the time-based RSUs awarded to non-employee directors lapse over a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year period. Time-based RSUs require <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> goals to be achieved other than the passage of time and continued employment. The restrictions on the performance-based restricted stock units lapse if we meet specific targets as defined. During the restricted period, the RSUs&#160;or RSAs&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be transferred or encumbered, but the recipient has the right to receive dividend equivalents and&#160;there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> voting rights until the award vests. If dividends are declared, dividend equivalents are accrued on performance-based restricted shares and ultimately paid only if the performance criteria are achieved. RSU and RSA compensation costs are recognized on a straight-line basis over the vesting period and are net of forfeitures.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">RSUs granted to officers and employees under the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan generally have a vesting period over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057709">three</span> years in equal installments from the date of grant, except that (i) the RSUs or RSAs granted to directors vest over <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057710">one</span> year and (ii) certain RSUs granted to our officers are performance based and vest on the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> anniversary of the date of grant, based on our performance as measured.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">The following table sets forth a summary of our RSU and RSA activity:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSharebasedCompensationRestrictedStockAndRestrictedStockUnitsActivityTableTextBlock" id="F078BC12-85A2-492E-A889-F3E1A4F93E98" escape="true" continuedAt="c6B207827-574F-4BBA-87E8-DDBA2334771A">

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:24pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em style="font: inherit;">11</em>)</b></p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;"><b>COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:24.5pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Currency Devaluation and Fluctuation Risk </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Due to our international operations,&#160;we are exposed to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations against the U.S. dollar. For some of our international contracts, a portion of the revenue and local expenses are incurred in local currencies with the result that we are at risk for changes in the exchange rates between the U.S. dollar and foreign currencies. To minimize the financial impact of these items, we attempt to contract a significant majority of our services in U.S. dollars. In addition, we attempt to minimize the financial impact of these risks by matching the currency of our operating costs with the currency of our revenue streams when considered appropriate. We continually monitor the currency exchange risks associated with all contracts <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> denominated in U.S. dollars.&#160;In recent years, laws impacting our operations in certain African countries&#160;require our customers to pay us onshore in local currency rather than offshore in U.S. dollars, subjecting us to heightened&#160;currency risk and restrictions on the repatriation of cash. As a result, we have accumulated foreign denominated cash in these countries. We continue to take steps to mitigate this additional foreign currency and repatriation risk with a focus on reducing cash balances denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar. Despite our efforts to mitigate currency risk, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>report significant realized and unrealized currency-related losses in our income statements.&#160;During the <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we entered into derivative contracts to assist us in managing our foreign currency risk.&#160;See Note&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">12</em>) -&#160;&#8220;Fair Value Measurements&#8221;&#160;and Note&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">13</em>) -&#160;&#8220;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#8221;&#160;for activity and disclosure related to our foreign currency derivative contracts.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Legal Proceedings </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2009,</em>&#160;on behalf of the Venezuelan government, Petr&#243;leos de Venezuela, S.A. (PDVSA), the national oil company of Venezuela, took possession of our assets and operations in Venezuela. In connection with this expropriation, we fully wrote-down our Venezuelan assets and initiated international arbitration. In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2019,</em>&#160;we converted our final international award into a U.S. federal court judgement, which we perfected pursuant to a writ of attachment against the shares held by PDVSA in PDV Holding, Inc. (PDVH), the parent company of CITGO Petroleum Corporation. The Delaware District Court (Court) ordered a public sale of the PDVH shares (the PDVH Sale) to satisfy the various judgments against Venezuela in&#160;<i>Crystallex International Corp. v. Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela</i>,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No.</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">17</em>-mc-<em style="font: inherit;">151</em>-LPS (D. Del.). On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 2, 2025,&#160;</em>the Court appointed Special Master filed its final recommendation for the winning bid for the PDVH Sale, which included listing the Tidewater subsidiaries holding judgment as the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> most senior creditors. On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 25, 2025, </em>the Court approved the Special Master&#8217;s recommended purchaser.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Closing of the PDVH Sale and the collection of our judgement, if at all, are highly uncertain and present significant practical and legal challenges, including, without limitation, satisfaction of numerous closing conditions, including regulatory approval by the Office of Foreign Assets Control, and the positive final outcome of numerous claims filed by other parties opposing the PDVH Sale.&#160;We can provide&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurances regarding the timing or ultimate outcome of this case. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the value of our judgment, including&#160;interest, was approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141057791" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedFromOtherParty" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">79.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. However, given the collection uncertainty, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;amount had been recorded in our financial statements related to this gain contingency.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;addition to the foregoing, we are named defendants or parties in certain lawsuits, claims or proceedings incidental to our business and involved from time to time as parties to governmental investigations or proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business. Although the outcome of such lawsuits or other proceedings cannot be predicted with certainty and the amount of any liability or gain that could arise with respect to such lawsuits or other proceedings cannot be predicted accurately, we do&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;expect these matters to have a material adverse effect on our financial position, operating results or cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 2%;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>(<em style="font: inherit;">12</em>) </b></p> </td><td style="width: 98%;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#160; FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p> </td></tr>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Other Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our primary financial instruments consist of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, trade receivables and trade payables with book values that are considered to be representative of their respective fair values.&#160;The carrying value for cash equivalents is considered to be representative of its fair value due to the short duration and conservative nature of the cash equivalent investment portfolio.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2022,</em> we agreed with PEMEX, the Mexican national oil company, to exchange $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057798" contextRef="i_2022-06-30_CounterpartyNameAxis-PemexMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableGrossCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.6</ix:nonFraction> million in accounts receivable for an equal face amount of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057799">seven</span>-year <ix:nonFraction id="c141057800" contextRef="i_2022-06-30_FinancialInstrumentAxis-ForeignCorporateDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">8.75</ix:nonFraction>% PEMEX corporate bonds (PEMEX Note). We sold approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057801" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-06-30_CounterpartyNameAxis-PemexMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableforsaleSecuritiesSoldAtPar" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of the PEMEX Notes during the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> half&#160;of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057804" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-PemexMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableforsaleSecuritiesSoldAtPar" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">8.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of the PEMEX Notes during <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> for their approximate book value.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We periodically enter into derivative contracts to manage our exposure to foreign currency risk. These derivative contracts, which are placed with major financial institutions, generally take the form of forward contracts with a duration of less than <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months. We report derivative instruments on the balance sheet as either assets or liabilities measured at fair value. Changes in fair value are recognized currently in earnings unless specific hedge accounting criteria are met. We generally do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designate our derivative instruments as hedges for accounting purposes, therefore, any gains or losses resulting from changes in fair value of outstanding derivative financial instruments and from the settlement of derivative financial instruments are recognized in earnings and included as a component of foreign exchange gains (losses) in the Consolidated Income Statements.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We held&#160;derivative instruments related to foreign exchange contracts recorded as&#160;prepaid expenses and other current assets and&#160;current liabilities, which were measured at their approximate fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057808" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-PrepaidExpensesAndOtherCurrentAssetsMember_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel2Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFairValueOfDerivativeNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057809" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherCurrentLiabilitiesMember_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel2Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFairValueOfDerivativeNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.&#160;</em>See Note&#160;(<em style="font: inherit;">13</em>) -&#160;&#8220;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#8221;&#160;for activity and disclosure related to our foreign currency derivative contracts.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Beginning in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> we entered into foreign currency contracts&#160;to sell Euros at future defined dates and at fixed exchange rates, to limit our exposure to losses related to the revaluation of non-USD cash balances held in certain African currencies that are marked to the Euro.&#160;We did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designate these contracts as hedges for accounting purposes.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Each of our <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057826"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057965">five</span></span> operating segments is led by senior management&#160;reporting to our Chief Executive Officer, the chief operating decision maker (CODM).&#160;Our operating segments comprise the structure used by our CODM to make key operating decisions and assess performance. Discrete financial information is available for each of the segments, and our Chief Executive Officer uses the results of each of the operating segments for resource allocation and performance evaluation.&#160;Our CODM evaluates the segments&#8217; operating performance based on segment operating income.&#160;Segment operating income is defined as segment revenues less segment costs and expenses. The CODM primarily considers segment operating income for evaluating performance of each segment and making decisions about allocating capital and other resources to each segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The following table provides a comparison of revenues, vessel operating profit, depreciation and amortization, additions to properties and equipment and assets by segment and in total. Vessel operating profit&#160;is calculated as vessel revenues less vessel operating costs, segment depreciation expenses, and segment general and administrative costs. Vessel revenues and operating costs relate to our owned and operated vessels while other operating revenues relate to the activities of our other miscellaneous marine-related businesses.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Acquisition of&#160;</i></b><i><b>Wilson Sons Ultratug Participa</b>&#231;&#245;<b>es S.A.</b><b>&#160;</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 22, 2026, </em>we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire all outstanding shares of Wilson Sons Ultratug Participa&#231;&#245;es S.A and its affiliate Atlantic Offshore Services S.A. (collectively, the Wilson Companies) from Wilson Sons S.A., Ultranav International II, S.A. and Remolcadores Ultratug Limitada (collectively, the Wilson Sellers). The Wilson Companies own <em style="font: inherit;">22</em> platform supply vessels operating in Brazil. We will pay the Wilson Sellers an aggregate cash purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057835" contextRef="d_2026-02-22_2026-02-22_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-TheWilsonCompaniesMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">500.0</ix:nonFraction> million on a debt free, cash free basis, subject to adjustments, including a reduction for the assumption of the Wilson Companies&#8217; debt which was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141057836" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_LegalEntityAxis-TheWilsonCompaniesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">261.0</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025. </em>The final debt amount will be determined upon completion of this transaction. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including approval from the Brazilian Antitrust Authority and the consent of the lenders to the Wilson Companies, and is expected to close late in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em></p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="Item9_Changes" title="Item9_Changes" href="#"></a>ITEM&#160;9. CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS ON ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">None.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="Item9A_Controls" title="Item9A_Controls" href="#"></a>ITEM&#160;9A. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Disclosure controls and procedures are designed with the objective of providing reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in our reports,&#160;filed or submitted under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act), such as this Annual Report on Form 10-K, is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our chief executive and chief financial officers, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. However, any control system, no matter how well conceived and followed, can provide only reasonable, and not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system are met.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of December 31, 2025, the end of the period covered by this report, we have evaluated, under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our President, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act, as amended). Based on that evaluation, our President, Chief Executive Officer, and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective at the reasonable assurance level.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><a id="Management" title="Management" href="#"></a>Management&#8217;s&#160;Report&#160;on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934). Our internal control over financial reporting was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation and financial statements for external purposes in accordance generally accepted accounting principles. Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025. In making this assessment, management used the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) in <i>Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).</i> Based on our assessment, our management concluded that, as of December 31, 2025, our internal control over financial reporting was&#160;effective based on those criteria.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025&#160;has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which appears herein.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="Item10_Directors" title="Item10_Directors" href="#"></a>ITEM&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> DIRECTORS, EXECUTIVE OFFICERS AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Directors and Executive Officers</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The information required by this Item&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057851">10</span> regarding the Company&#8217;s directors will be set forth under the heading &#8220;Proposal <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> - Election of Directors&#8221; in the Proxy Statement for the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Annual Meeting of Stockholders and is incorporated herein by reference. The information required by this Item&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> regarding the Company&#8217;s executive officers will be set forth under the heading &#8220;Proposal <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Advisory Vote to Approve our Executive Compensation&#8221; and is incorporated herein by reference</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Section</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">16</em>(a) Compliance</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">If applicable, the information required by this Item&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> regarding compliance with Section&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">16</em>(a) of the Exchange Act will be set forth under the heading &#8220;Delinquent Section&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">16</em>(a) Reports&#8221; in the Proxy Statement for the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Annual Meeting of Stockholders and is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Corporate Governance</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Except as set forth in the following paragraph, the remaining information required by this Item&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> will be set forth under the heading &#8220;Corporate Governance&#8221; in the Proxy Statement for the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Annual Meeting of Stockholders and is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has adopted a Code of Business Conduct &amp; Ethics (Code) that applies to its principal executive officer, principal financial officer, and principal accounting officer or controller. The Company&#8217;s Code, as well as its Corporate Governance Guidelines and the charters of its Audit, Compensation &amp; Human Capital, Safety &amp; Sustainability, and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committees, are available on the Company&#8217;s website, www.tdw.com. Copies of these documents are also available upon request to Investor Relations, Tidewater Inc., <em style="font: inherit;">842</em> W. Sam Houston Parkway N., Suite <em style="font: inherit;">400,</em> Houston, Texas <em style="font: inherit;">77024.</em> The Company intends to disclose any amendments to, or waivers from, its Code that apply to the Company&#8217;s principal executive officer, principal financial officer, and principal accounting officer or controller on the Company&#8217;s website, www.tdw.com, under the&#160;&#8220;About&#160;Tidewater -&#160;Corporate Governance&#8221; caption, promptly following the date of any such amendment or waiver.&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><a id="Item11_Executive" title="Item11_Executive" href="#"></a>ITEM&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">11.</em> EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The information required by this Item&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141057867">11</span> will be set forth under the heading &#8220;Proposal <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Advisory Vote to Approve our Executive Compensation&#8221; in the Proxy Statement for the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Annual Meeting of Stockholders and is incorporated herein by reference.&#160;&#160;</p>
  </div>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><a id="Item12_Security" title="Item12_Security" href="#"></a>ITEM&#160;12. SECURITY OWNERSHIP OF CERTAIN BENEFICIAL OWNERS AND MANAGEMENT AND RELATED STOCKHOLDER MATTERS </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We permit our employees, officers and directors to enter into written trading plans complying with Rule 10b5-1 under the Exchange Act. Rule 10b5-1 provides criteria under which such an individual may establish a prearranged plan to buy or sell a specified number of shares of a company's stock over a set period of time. Persons using such plan must act in good faith with respect to the contract with the broker executing the trades, trading instructions and the trading plan as a whole. Such plan must be established at a time when the individual is not in possession of material, nonpublic information and will be subject to a cooling off period to the initial trade thereunder. If an individual establishes a plan satisfying the requirements of Rule 10b5-1, such individual's subsequent receipt of material, nonpublic information will not prevent transactions under the plan from being executed. Certain of our officers have advised us that they have and may enter into stock sales plans for the sale of shares of our common stock, which are intended to comply with the requirements of Rule 10b5-1 of the Exchange Act. In addition, the Company has and may in the future enter into repurchases of our common stock under a plan that complies with Rule 10b5-1 or Rule 10b-18 of the Exchange Act.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The additional information required by this Item&#160;12 will be set forth under the headings &#8220;Equity Compensation Plan Information&#8221;, &#8220;Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners&#8221; and &#8220;Security Ownership of Management:&#8221; in the Proxy Statement for the Company&#8217;s 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders and is incorporated herein by reference.</p>
